summary: Nacogdoches County, TX Texas Forest Service site listed as gone; a 1949 NGS note on the Etoile page names Etoile Lookout Tower No. 6 without tying it to Loc 1.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Texas list; no removal date in the sources read

evidence.supports: Etoile (Loc 1) listed in Nacagdoches County at 31.36111, -94.38861, as a tower that is gone
Etoile (Loc 2) is a separate site listed as standing
county spelled Nacogdoches County on the Forest Lookouts page
agency is the Texas Forest Service
page reproduces a National Geodetic Survey station description

evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1949

evidence.supports: survey mark sits on the summit of a high hill
evidence.quote: ON THE SUMMIT OF A HIGH HILL

evidence.supports: mark is 89.59 feet northwest of the center of the named tower
the description names Etoile Lookout Tower No. 6
mark is stamped with the name Etoile and the year 1949
page content is a National Geodetic Survey station description rather than a tower history

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts Etoile page gives the county as Nacogdoches County; the record's spelling is a misspelling of that name

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Texas list spells the county Nacagdoches; the Forest Lookouts Etoile page spells it Nacogdoches. The story uses the page's spelling and notes the list's.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and neither describes the Loc 1 tower itself. The Forest Lookouts Etoile page reproduces an NGS station description that names Etoile Lookout Tower No. 6; nothing ties that tower to Loc 1 or Loc 2, so the story says so and does not assume it. WebSearch found no Etoile-specific history. Leads for a later pass: the Cavallerano book Fire in the Piney Woods (Texas A&M University Press, 2025) and Texas A&M Forest Service archives. The Lufkin Daily News and tfsweb.tamu.edu pages could not be fetched (HTTP 429 and 403).
